fields.v: Saxena, S., Trivedi, N., Jyothi, V. (2026). SWE-WebDevBench: Evaluating Coding Agent Application Platforms as Virtual Software Agencies. arXiv:2605.04637v1 [cs.MA], 6 May 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2605.04637v1 [cs.MA], 6 May 2026 (dated March 2026 on the title page); no venue stated
BaseThesis Labs (Saxena); QwikBuild (Trivedi, Jyothi), the vendor of one of the six evaluated platforms (conflict of interest disclosed)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — SWE-WebDev Bench, a 68-metric framework (25 primary, 43 diagnostic, 7 groups) along Interaction Mode (ACR/AMR), Agency Angle (PM/Engineering/Ops) and Complexity Tier (T4/T5), with canary requirements; six AI app-building platforms compared on three ACR prompts, AMR shown for one platform

Six commercial AI app-building platforms (snapshot February-March 2026; underlying models not stated): Base44 (low-code generator), Emergent E1-OPUS (agentic with config Q&A), Lovable in Plan Mode (plan-then-build), QwikBuild (multi-agent with a PM agent; authors' affiliation), Replit Agent3 (autonomous agent), Vercel v0-Max (single-shot generation)

Not prescribed by the benchmark; observed platform artefacts: QwikBuild 12-section PRD (Product Overview, Scope v0/v1, Features, Roles, Data Model, Auth, Dashboards, Background Jobs, Acceptance Criteria, Risks & Open Questions, Handoff Notes) and execution plan; Base44 plan with 'Intent & Goal', 'Audience & Roles', 'Core Flows', 'What NOT to Do'; v0-Max TodoManager task breakdown. Benchmark inputs: business prompts with embedded canary requirements and deliberate contradictions

Platform flow: prompt -> PM clarification (0-15 questions; 0 for Replit and Base44 on P1/P3) -> PRD/plan -> build -> deploy; AMR: modification prompt -> change acknowledgment -> plan update -> code. Evaluation protocol (7 phases, 14 days per platform x prompt): build execution, code quality audit, integration and security testing, feature and canary testing, AMR change injection, human panel and cost aggregation, diagnostic scoring

User (evaluator) answers platform clarification questions and resolves flagged contradictions (e.g. QwikBuild integrates the user's choice into the PRD before building); human re-prompts and manual edits after generation counted as PHE
Full workflow of each platform (requirement elicitation to deployment); AMR (modification) only for QwikBuild
Not classifiable; authors' wording: 'specification bottleneck', 'Post-PRD human effort', 'closed-loop code generation' where build-time discoveries feed back into planning
New project (ACR: full-stack application from a natural-language business prompt) and existing code base (AMR: modification of the deployed ACR application; QwikBuild only)

6 prompts (3 ACR, 3 AMR) in 3 domains; 6 platforms; 18 ACR evaluation cells plus 3 AMR cells (QwikBuild); 80 canary requirements (21 Original, 37 New, 18 Surviving, 4 Contradiction); complexity tiers T4 (multi-role SaaS) and T5 (AI-native)

Business web applications: EdTech (Indian coaching institute, JEE/NEET), Field Service (10-state ticket lifecycle, SLA, GST invoicing), FinTech-AI (multi-stage AI analysis, Monte Carlo, credit system)

Target user: non-technical business user (prompts written as founder message, enterprise RFP, complex specification); evaluators: the authors (two affiliated with QwikBuild) and a three-person expert panel including one external evaluator; not blinded

Total Cost of Correctness (TCC: platform billing, compute time and human effort as one monetary figure; values not given in the main tables); Effort-to-Fix (ETF) and Feature Gap Delta (FGD) in developer-hours; build time noted anecdotally (v0-Max timed out at 10m37s on P2)

Feature Completeness Score (FCS); Core Integration Score (CIS); External Service Reliability (ESR); Cron & Background Jobs Score (CBS); AI-Inside-App (AIA); Code Change Impact Score (CCIS); regressions and new features working (AMR); deployment success

Schema Design (SDS), Backend Logic (BLS), Frontend Engineering (FES), Code Hygiene (CHS), Architecture (ARC); Security Score (SS, OWASP Top 10), Scalability Architecture (SAS), Concurrency & Load (CLS, k6); Engineering Score = weighted mean of G2-G6

Effort-to-Fix (ETF, developer-hours to production quality, expert panel); Post-PRD Human Effort (PHE: re-prompts and hours of manual code edits); Feature Gap Delta (FGD, developer-hours for missing features)

Business Intent Fidelity (BIF), Canary Retention Rate (CRR), Claim Drift Index (CDI), SEO & Web Standards (SWS), Lead & Growth (LGS), Multilingual (MLS), AI Feature Quality (AFQ); 43 diagnostics incl. Explicit Capture Rate, Inference Quality Score, Conversational Guidance, Under-Clarification Rate, Plan Structural Validity, contradiction detection, Adaptive Coherence Score, Change Acknowledgment and Plan Update Rates, per-stage canary survival

Four judge tiers: Tier 0 automated (HTTP endpoint tests, Lighthouse, k6, npm audit; ~40% of Engineering Score); Tier 1 LLM judge (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, temperature 0, 9 prompt templates, platform identity hidden; kappa 0.82 vs a human on 36 items); Tier 2 LLM + human validation (kappa 0.71 on 18 items); Tier 3 three-person expert panel (kappa 0.64) for BIF, ETF, FGD. Manual verification of FCS and CRR against the reference specification; TCC from billing and effort logs

Criterion: authors' per-metric 'aspirational' targets (Engineering Score 60%, FCS 85, CRR 80, SS 90, CLS 70, ETF <=16 h, FGD <=40 h, CDI <=10), described as the minimum for production deployment but 'not to define pass/fail gates'; the authors nevertheless report pass/fail against them ('fails 17 of 22 metrics'). ACR averages over P1-P3 (Engineering Score; FCS; CRR; SS; CBS; ETF h; FGD h; CDI %): (a) Base44: 30.6; 46.7; 24.3; 31.3; 15.0; 65.7; 29.3; 35.7. (b) Emergent E1-OPUS: 46.9; 65.0; 57.0; 50.7; 20.3; 26.0; 19.0; 17.7. (c) Lovable Plan Mode: 42.5; 32.7; 21.7; 51.7; 2.0; 50.7; 36.3; 37.3. (d) QwikBuild: 54.5; 84.0; 97.7; 63.7; 49.3; 14.7; 9.3; 4.0. (e) Replit Agent3: 47.8; 53.0; 54.0; 40.0; 29.7; 37.3; 25.7; 14.0. (f) v0-Max: 25.1; 23.3; 17.7; 34.3; 0.0; 54.7; 41.7; 33.7. Quality verdict against the authors' targets: does not work for all six (no Engineering Score >= 60; no platform passes more than 5 of 22 metrics). Cost: TCC defined but no values reported, so no cost verdict; effort targets give mixed results (ETF <= 16 h met only by QwikBuild, 14.7 h; FGD <= 40 h met by all except v0-Max, 41.7 h). (g) QwikBuild AMR (P4-P6, scored by affiliated authors): zero regressions; ACS 84% (P4) to 90% (P6) vs 85% target; new features working 12/15, 7/9, 8/9; most metrics 1-24 pp below ACR (CBS -24.3, CRR -14.0)

Tasks: same six prompts (3 ACR with different authoring styles, 3 AMR) on all platforms for ACR. Configurations: six platforms; AMR only QwikBuild. Baseline: none; authors' target thresholds as reference. Held constant: prompts, canary requirements, 7-phase protocol, LLM judge and rubrics. Not controlled: underlying models, platform tiers, evaluator blinding. Acceptance: automated tests (HTTP, Lighthouse, k6, npm audit) plus LLM and expert judgement against a reference specification. Repetitions: one run per cell; no significance tests or CIs (authors estimate 15-20 prompts in 5-7 domains needed). Human intervention: evaluator answers platform questions; re-prompts counted

QwikBuild highest Engineering Score (54.5%), then Replit (47.8), Emergent (46.9), Lovable (42.5), Base44 (30.6), v0-Max (25.1); no platform above 60%; descriptive only, no significance tests. CRR 17.7-97.7%; IQS 20-70; Frontend Engineering within 6 points for four platforms (68-74%) while CBS ranges 0-49%; best Security Score 63.7% (target 90), CLS 6-42%; ETF 14.7-65.7 developer-hours. All six detected the marked P2 contradiction, three asked the user to resolve it; only one detected the unmarked P1 contradiction. Domain swings up to 13 points (Replit P1 41.5 vs P3 54.5). v0-Max highest SWS (40.3%) despite lowest Engineering Score

Distinguished platforms and surfaced per-platform blind spots; 42% of metric pairs weakly correlated (|tau| <= 0.40), groups not independent factors. Repeatability: single snapshot and single run, small calibration samples (kappa 0.82/0.71/0.64). Limitations stated: conflict of interest and no blinding; single evaluator for some metrics; small sample; platform version sensitivity; AMR only for one platform; prompt wording and benchmark emphasis on PM behaviour and T4/T5 complexity may favour platforms with PM agents

Limitations: author affiliation with QwikBuild; no blinding; single evaluator for some metrics; six prompts, no inferential statistics; snapshot Feb-Mar 2026; AMR asymmetry; prompt sensitivity; design may favour certain architectures. Gaps: requirement elicitation and specification fidelity, backend infrastructure (background jobs, external services), security hardening, code hygiene, web standards; closed-loop code generation proposed; need for independent, blinded, larger-scale replications

Inconsistencies: Figure 4 caption calls the CRR range (17.7-97.7%) a '3.5x variation in inference quality', while the text gives 5.5x for CRR and 3.5x for IQS; Figure 2 caption says canaries are 'embedded across 9 prompts' vs six prompts elsewhere; Table 12 shows no Engineering Score for Base44 on P1 ('-') while Table 5 gives 30.2; §5.6 says AMR scores are '1-14 pp' below ACR but CBS drops 24.3 pp; title page dated March 2026, arXiv v1 6 May 2026. Claims without analysis: PM elicitation 'accounts for approximately 10-15% of the observed quality gap'; 'strongly predicts downstream quality'. AMR results scored by QwikBuild-affiliated authors. Values from Tables 5, 6, 8, 12, 14, 15 (pp. 14, 17, 21, 24-25). Table 6 FGD and CDI rows rebuilt from jumbled text by position (targets <=40 and <=10, then six values each in platform order B0, E1, L0, Q1, R3, V0); consistent with the P1 values in Tables 12 and 16 and with the text (Base44 CDI 35%). Table 16 places ETF in G7, while Table 2 puts it in G5. Data: prompts, 80 canary specifications, 9 judge prompts, raw scores (CSV), rubrics and anonymisation scripts at github.com/snowmountainAi/webdevbench. Pre-registration: not stated. Programming languages: not stated (generated full-stack web apps; npm ecosystem mentioned)
